notes: The Allegory of the Cave interlude (Plato, Republic VII 514a–518b, paraphrased; no long quotation).
chained: You cannot turn your head. You never could.
On the wall in front of you, shapes pass: a horse, a jar, a man, a tree. They are the only things you have ever seen.
The others beside you name them as they pass, and praise whoever guesses best what comes next.
turned: Someone loosens the chains. 'Stand up. Turn around.'
Behind you, a fire. It hurts to look at. The shadows were easier.
Between you and the fire runs a low wall, and men walk along it holding things up above it.

objects.horse: A carved horse of wood. Its shadow is what you called 'a horse' all your life.
objects.vase: A painted jar. Its shadow had no colour. You had no idea it had colour.
objects.man: A stone figure of a man. And the men carrying it are not shadows at all.
objects.tree: A little tree cut from leather, held up on a stick. Is this, then, what a tree is?

dragged: A hand grips your arm and pulls you, past the fire, toward a rough steep passage climbing into the dark.
ascent: The way up is steep and rough. You do not want to go. Your guide does not let go.
outside: Light. Too much light. You can see nothing at all.
Wait. Let your eyes get used to it. Look down first, at the ground.

seen.shadow: Shadows on the grass, sharp and clear. These, at least, you understand.
seen.reflection: In the still pool, the tree and the sky, upside down. Reflections are easier than the things themselves.
seen.things: The tree itself. Bark, leaves, a bird in the branches. Real, and more real than anything below.
seen.sun: And at last the sun: not its reflection in water, but the sun itself, in its own place. The cause of the seasons and the years, and in a way of everything you used to see.

tooBright: Too bright. You look away, eyes streaming. Not yet.
choice: You remember the cave, and the others still chained there, naming shadows.
Would you go back down to free them? They would laugh at you. They might kill you.
descend: You go back down. After the sun, the cave is black. You stumble; you cannot see the shadows at all.
'He went up, and came back with his eyes ruined,' they say. 'Better never to go up.'
But your eyes will get used to the dark again. And then you will see the shadows better than any of them, because you know what they are shadows of.
stay: You stay in the light. Nobody below will ever know what you saw.
Is that wisdom, or is it selfishness? The question follows you back down into sleep.
